title: University of Chicago students rally against sexual violence and fraternities
seoTitle: Chicago UChicago protest against sexual violence

tea.why: Students and staff protested following recent allegations of sexual assaults involving fraternities near the campus.
tea.want: Demonstrators demanded that the university address a list of safety and disciplinary demands by November 20.
tea.changed: Oct 28: Dozens of students and community members rallied for an hour on the university's Main Quadrangle.

summary: Students, staff, and community members gathered on the main quadrangle of the University of Chicago to protest against sexual violence and campus fraternity culture. The demonstration followed recent allegations involving fraternity houses near the campus, including an October 11 incident at Alpha Epsilon Pi and a February incident at Alpha Delta Phi that led to a lawsuit. Participants chanted slogans and displayed posters demanding institutional action and accountability. Organizers outlined several demands for the university to meet by November 20, including mandatory minimum consequences for sexual violence, student-approved training developers, and an independent audit of the campus police and Title IX office. The university has previously stated that the fraternities are not formally affiliated with the institution.
demands: Revisions to the disciplinary policy to establish mandatory minimum consequences for sexual violence
Hiring a third-party curriculum developer for mandatory sexual assault awareness training
Conducting an independent audit of the university police department practices and prior investigations
Reviewing the university's Title IX office and student conduct matters
response: No official university response was detailed in the sources regarding the rally, though the university has previously stated that the fraternities are not formally affiliated with the institution.
